rules.title: Creating a player character
rules.summary: Generate abilities using the method your DM permits, then choose race, class and alignment and record languages, money, equipment and hit points.
bullets: Keep a character record with possessions, spells and cumulative XP.
Race and class eligibility must be checked before choices are finalized.

rules.title: The six ability scores
rules.summary: Strength, intelligence, wisdom, dexterity, constitution and charisma describe different capabilities. The DM chooses the method used to generate them.
bullets: Ability requirements can restrict race or class choices.
Consult each ability's own adjustments rather than applying a universal modifier.

rules.title: Strength and exceptional strength
rules.summary: Strength affects melee accuracy, damage, carrying allowance and forcing obstacles. Fighters with strength 18 roll percentile dice for exceptional strength.
bullets: The exceptional-strength table is restricted to fighters in this PHB rule.
Fighters with strength 16 or higher receive a 10% earned-XP bonus.

Weight allowance adjusts the normal unencumbered allowance, measured in gold-piece weight (10 gp = 1 lb). Parenthesized door chances are out of six for fighters forcing locked, barred, magically held or wizard-locked doors: only one attempt per door is allowed. Bend-bars/lift-gates attempts are also one-time attempts.

rules.title: Intelligence and learning spells
rules.summary: Intelligence limits a magic-user's spell levels and spells known. Learning checks use percentile dice against the applicable chance-to-know entry.
bullets: A successful check determines whether the spell can be learned when found.
The minimum-spells rule permits rechecking failed spells until the minimum is met.
Stop learning in that spell-level group when the maximum is reached.
Additional languages by Intelligence: 3–7: 0; 8–9: 1; 10–11: 2; 12–13: 3; 14–15: 4; 16: 5; 17: 6; 18: 7. Nonhuman language rules and racial limits also apply.

Magic-user spell learning rows are Intelligence: chance to know each listed spell / minimum spells per spell level / maximum spells per spell level: 9: 35%/4/6; 10–12: 45%/5/7; 13–14: 55%/6/9; 15–16: 65%/7/11; 17: 75%/8/14; 18: 85%/9/18; 19 or more: 95%/10/all.
Minimum Intelligence to use magic-user spells of levels 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 is respectively 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18.

rules.title: Wisdom: bonus spells and spell failure
rules.summary: Wisdom's clerical bonus spells are cumulative, but become available only when the cleric can already cast that spell level. Low wisdom can cause spell failure.
bullets: The magical-attack adjustment applies to mental attacks involving willpower, not every saving throw.
A failed clerical spell is expended with no effect.
Magical-attack saving-throw adjustment by Wisdom: 3 −3; 4 −2; 5–7 −1; 8–14 none; 15 +1; 16 +2; 17 +3; 18 +4. This applies to mental attack forms involving will force.

Cleric bonus spell increments and failure chance by Wisdom: 9 none/20%; 10 none/15%; 11 none/10%; 12 none/5%; 13 one 1st-level/0%; 14 one 1st-level/0%; 15 one 2nd-level/0%; 16 one 2nd-level/0%; 17 one 3rd-level/0%; 18 one 4th-level/0%. Bonus increments accumulate and require access to the spell level. Wisdom 17 is the minimum for 6th-level cleric spells and 18 for 7th-level spells.

rules.title: Dexterity: surprise, missiles and defense
rules.summary: Dexterity has separate reaction/attacking and defensive adjustments, plus a separate table for thief functions.
bullets: The reaction/attacking adjustment applies to surprise and missile attacks.
Defensive benefits depend on being able to react or dodge; use the applicable combat rules.
Add relevant racial thief adjustments to the ability adjustments.
Dexterity rows are score: reaction/missile attack adjustment / defensive adjustment: 3 −3/+4; 4 −2/+3; 5 −1/+2; 6 0/+1; 7–14 0/0; 15 0/−1; 16 +1/−2; 17 +2/−3; 18 +3/−4.

Thief Dexterity adjustments, in percentage points for pick pockets/open locks/find-remove traps/move silently/hide in shadows: 9 −15/−10/−10/−20/−10; 10 −10/−5/−10/−15/−5; 11 −5/0/−5/−10/0; 12 0/0/0/−5/0; 13–15 0/0/0/0/0; 16 0/+5/0/0/0; 17 +5/+10/0/+5/+5; 18 +10/+15/+5/+10/+10. Apply these to base chances; racial adjustments are additional.

rules.title: Constitution and hit points
rules.summary: Apply the constitution hit-point adjustment to each hit die; a penalty cannot reduce a die below 1 hit point.
bullets: Under this PHB rule, only fighters, including paladins and rangers, receive constitution bonuses above +2 per die.
System shock and resurrection survival are different percentage checks.

The initial Constitution score caps the number of raise-dead or resurrection revivifications, and each such revivification reduces Constitution by 1. Increasing or restoring Constitution does not raise that original limit. The text notes that other magic such as wish may provide another means.

rules.title: Resurrection survival and lifetime limit
rules.summary: The initial constitution score limits the number of times a character can be raised or resurrected. Each revival also reduces constitution by 1.
bullets: Magically improving constitution does not replenish that original lifetime limit.
The resurrection-survival percentage is a separate requirement.

rules.summary: Charisma determines the maximum number of permanent henchmen and adjusts loyalty and encounter reactions.
bullets: The henchman maximum does not limit ordinary paid servants or mercenary soldiers.
Charisma includes persuasion and personal presence as well as appearance.

rules.title: Race, class eligibility and level limits
rules.summary: The PHB offers dwarf, elf, gnome, half-elf, halfling, half-orc and human characters. Racial tables restrict classes and, for many non-human classes, advancement.
bullets: Your DM may restrict available races for the campaign.
UA provides additional racial choices and revised limits; keep the selected source explicit.

PHB class level table (U = unlimited; parenthesized entries are non-player characters only; omitted classes are unavailable to that race): dwarf fighter 9, thief U, assassin 9, cleric (8); elf fighter 7, magic-user 11, thief U, assassin 10, cleric (7); gnome fighter 6, illusionist 7, thief U, assassin 8, cleric (7); half-elf cleric 5, druid U, fighter 8, ranger 8, magic-user 8, thief U, assassin 11; halfling fighter 6, thief U, druid (6); half-orc cleric 4, fighter 10, thief 8, assassin U; human all listed classes U. All are still subject to applicable ability and class requirements.

PHB fighter limits by Strength: dwarf below 17 → 7, at 17 → 8, otherwise maximum 9; elf below 17 → 5, at 17 → 6, otherwise maximum 7; gnome below 18 → 5, otherwise 6; half-elf below 17 → 6, at 17 → 7, otherwise 8. Halfling Hairfeet and others under Strength 17 → 4; Tallfellows at 17 and Stouts at 18 → 5; Tallfellows with 18 → 6.

PHB magic-user limits by Intelligence: elf below 17 → 9, at 17 → 10, otherwise maximum 11; half-elf below 17 → 6, at 17 → 7, otherwise maximum 8. Gnome illusionists with Intelligence or Dexterity below 17 are limited to 5; with both 17 to 6; otherwise table maximum 7. Half-orc thieves with Dexterity below 17 are limited to 6, at 17 to 7, otherwise maximum 8.
The printed half-elven ranger 8 entry bears footnote 4, but that footnote explicitly describes half-elven fighters. The table’s application of that footnote to rangers is unresolved.

rules.title: Humans changing class
rules.summary: A human may stop advancing in one profession and begin another, subject to ability and alignment requirements. This differs from simultaneous non-human multiclassing.
bullets: Required principal abilities are at least 15 in the original class and 17 in the new class.
Using the former class's functions before surpassing its level forfeits XP for that adventure.
Once the new level exceeds the old, class functions may be combined subject to equipment restrictions.

bullets: A paladin is lawful good; a druid is true neutral under these PHB rules.

rules.summary: Hit points combine physical resilience with skill, luck and supernatural protection. Restoring lost points cannot raise the character beyond their established total.
bullets: Hit-die type and exceptional starting dice depend on class.

rules.summary: One gold piece equals 20 silver pieces, 200 copper pieces or 2 electrum pieces. One platinum piece equals 5 gold pieces.
bullets: Coin denominations are assumed to have similar size and weight.

rules.title: Armor class and magical protection
rules.summary: Armor and shields establish a base AC, with dexterity and magic modifying it. Lower numeric armor classes offer better protection.
bullets: Unarmored is AC 10; plate mail with a shield is AC 2 in this table.
Each +1 of magic armor or shield decreases AC by 1.
A monster's AC may represent hide, agility or other defenses rather than worn armor.
Base AC without shield: leather or padded 8; studded leather or ring mail 7; scale 6; chain 5; splint or banded 4; plate 3.
A shield improves these listed armor classes by one when applicable; shield alone is AC 9.

rules.title: When a shield protects you

bullets: Small shield: one attack; normal shield: two; large shield: three.

rules.title: Wandering and placed encounters
rules.summary: Wandering encounters occur through encounter checks; placed encounters arise from the DM's keyed locations. Unnecessary time and noise can attract more danger.

Negotiation or avoidance can be useful alternatives to combat.
For an Appendix C dungeon character-party encounter, roll d4 + 1 for 2–5 characters; accompanying men-at-arms or henchmen bring the total party to nine.

rules.title: Encounter and combat sequence
rules.summary: Establish surprise and distance, determine initiative when applicable, then resolve the sides' chosen actions. Repeat distance, initiative and action while the encounter continues.
bullets: Actions may include avoiding contact, parley, missiles, spells, closing, charging or melee.
A minute-long melee round represents maneuvering and unsuccessful attempts as well as scored blows.

rules.title: Tied initiative and damage timing

bullets: A large weapon-speed difference can permit additional attacks under the DMG procedure.
Multiple attack routines and charges have their own ordering rules.

rules.title: Morale and losing the will to fight
rules.summary: Morale checks can govern non-leader NPCs, hirelings, henchmen and intelligent opponents. Casualties, lost leadership and superior enemy force can trigger checks.
bullets: Check each round against an obviously superior force. Apply +5% at 25% party casualties, +10% if the leader is unconscious, +15% at 50% or more casualties, and +30% if the leader is slain or deserts; the casualty thresholds also apply to individual wounds.

Modifiers: each enemy deserting −5%, each enemy slain −10%, inflicting casualties without receiving any −20%, each friend killed +10%, taking casualties without inflicting any +10%, each friend deserting +15%, and being outnumbered and outclassed at least 3 to 1 +20%.
Roll percentile dice against the creature’s morale or loyalty score after adjustments; the amount by which the adjusted roll exceeds the score determines the failure outcome.
Failure by 1–15% means fall back fighting; 16–30% disengage and retreat; 31–50% flee in panic; 51% or more surrender.

rules.title: Zero hit points and emergency aid
rules.summary: At 0 hit points a creature becomes unconscious under this DMG procedure, then loses 1 point per following round until death at −10. Immediate aid stops that continuing loss.
bullets: The text optionally allows the triggering blow to leave the creature as low as −3.
After revival: 1d6 turns of coma and at least one week of rest; ordinary cures do not remove the restriction, but heal does.
More severe negative totals can have lasting consequences at the DM's option.

rules.title: Mentors, self-training and interruption

rules.title: Comeliness is separate from charisma
rules.summary: UA adds comeliness for physical appearance and initial reactions. Charisma still governs the longer-term interpersonal relationship once a character is known.
bullets: Roll 3d6 for base comeliness after the first six abilities. Charisma modifiers: below 3 −8; 3 −5; 4–5 −3; 6–8 −1; 9–12 0; 13–15 +1; 16–17 +2; 18 +3; above 18 +5. Later gains or losses of charisma adjust comeliness point for point.

Racial adjustment applies to reactions from other races: half-orc −3; dwarf or gnome −1; halfling or human 0; half-elf or sylvan elf +1; gray or high elf +2. Treat each starred pair as the same race for this purpose.

The following reaction bands concern creatures of human sort. At −16 or below, viewers recoil, flee or may attack; if viewer and subject are both evil, treat the score as positive. At −15 to −9, viewers show disgust and hostility; if all are evil, the negative score can be regarded as positive. At −8 to 0, viewers feel aversion and may become openly hostile.

At 1–6, viewers tend toward unease; enough conversation can let charisma offset it. At 7–9, the initial reaction is negative but high charisma can quickly overcome it. At 10–13, appearance has no effect on the viewer.
At 14–17, initial reaction improves by a percentage equal to the score; members of the opposite sex are affected as by fascination unless their Wisdom exceeds half the score.

At 18–21, initial reaction improves by 150% of the score. Opposite-sex viewers are affected as by fascination unless Wisdom exceeds two-thirds the score; same-sex viewers are similarly affected unless Wisdom is at least half the score. Harsh rejection can cause the rejected individual to react as if the subject had negative comeliness equal to half the positive score.

At 22–25, the reaction adjustment is twice the score. Fascination affects those with Wisdom less than two-thirds of the score; a consciously sought opposite-sex individual is fascinated unless Wisdom is 18 or higher. Harsh rejection has the same effect as in the 18–21 band.

At 26–30, reserved for unusual extraplanar demigods or deities, the reaction adjustment is twice the score. Fascination applies except to those with Wisdom at least 75% of the score, and Wisdom 19 or higher always permits a saving throw. A consciously sought opposite-sex individual is affected unless Wisdom is 20 or higher.

Fascination allows a saving throw versus spell; nonmagical comeliness fascination is not removed by dispel magic or antimagic. A fascinated creature follows an order if 3d6 does not exceed the subject’s comeliness: add 1 to the roll for requests against its interest, up to +6 or more for hazardous requests; a higher roll breaks fascination. Treatment during fascination affects subsequent reaction.

Comeliness is temporary as a reaction factor: once the subject is known, use charisma. Fascination does not prevent fighting or spellcasting or make the subject a puppet. Change self and alter self adjust comeliness by at most 1 point; an illusion of a high-comeliness creature works for one round; polymorph changes it by 2 points; shapechange gives the final form’s full effect.

rules.title: UA weapon specialization
rules.summary: Fighters and rangers can choose weapon specialization at creation. It normally uses two proficiency slots; a non-crossbow bow requires an additional slot.
bullets: Only fighters and rangers may specialize, choosing at character creation. Specialization costs two proficiency slots; a non-crossbow bow requires one additional slot. The weapon must be a specific type.
Melee specialization grants +1 to hit and +2 damage in addition to applicable Strength and magic bonuses. Other missile weapons also grant +1 to hit and +2 damage.

Bow point blank is 6–30 feet: +2 to hit and damage and double damage on a hit; the source gives 6–16 damage for a nonmagical arrow, plus applicable Strength or magic bonuses. At short range, beginning at 30 feet up to the lower limit of medium range, the specialist gains +1 to hit and damage. A nocked and drawn bow with target in sight may fire before initiative.

Crossbow point blank is 6–60 feet: +2 to hit and damage and double damage, with a 6–12 nonmagical light-crossbow example excluding Strength or magic bonuses. At short range gain +1 to hit and damage; at medium gain +1 to hit with no specialization damage bonus. A cocked and aimed crossbow with target in range gains a shot before initiative.

Specialist attacks per round at levels 1–6 / 7–12 / 13+: melee 3/2, 2/1, 5/2; bow 2/1, 3/1, 4/1; light crossbow 1/1, 3/2, 2/1; heavy crossbow 1/2, 1/1, 3/2; lasso or staff sling 1/1, 3/2, 2/1; thrown dagger 3/1, 4/1, 5/1; thrown dart 4/1, 5/1, 6/1; other missiles or hurled weapons 3/2, 2/1, 5/2. The table supersedes ordinary fighter/ranger attacks for the specialized weapon.

Double specialization costs another proficiency slot when a character qualifies for a new weapon, and must be in the weapon already specialized in. Only melee weapons qualify, excluding pole arms and the two-handed sword; it gives +3 to hit and +3 damage with that weapon.
Specialization hit bonuses are not magical and do not affect creatures hit only by magical weapons; applicable magical weapon bonuses are additional.

rules.title: Apply racial ability adjustments in order
rules.summary: A non-human or part-human character must meet the race's ability minimums. Apply racial bonuses and penalties before enforcing the race's maximum scores.
bullets: Minimums may be met by the initial roll plus the race's permitted bonus.
A score above a racial maximum is reduced to that maximum.
Check the selected printing and UA revisions before finalizing a character.

PHB racial ability limits below show each ability as minimum–maximum. A maximum written M/F gives the male maximum first and female maximum second; otherwise both are the same. Apply racial adjustments before the maximum; qualifying minimums can include an applicable racial bonus.
Dwarf: Strength 8–18/17; Intelligence 3–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 3–17; Constitution 12–19; Charisma 3–16.
Elf: Strength 3–18/16; Intelligence 8–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 7–19; Constitution 6–18; Charisma 8–18.
Gnome: Strength 6–18/15; Intelligence 7–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 3–18; Constitution 8–18; Charisma 3–18.
Half-elf: Strength 3–18/17; Intelligence 4–18; Wisdom 3–18; Dexterity 6–18; Constitution 6–18; Charisma 3–18.
Halfling: Strength 6–17/14; Intelligence 6–18; Wisdom 3–17; Dexterity 8–18; Constitution 10–19; Charisma 3–18.
Half-orc: Strength 6–18; Intelligence 3–17; Wisdom 3–14; Dexterity 3–17; Constitution 13–19; Charisma 3–12.

The PHB notes that fighters of all races might qualify for exceptional Strength; see the Strength table. This table covers the six listed nonhuman and part-human races; class requirements remain separate.
The dwarf Charisma maximum applies with respect to non-dwarves; the half-orc maximum applies with respect to non-orcs and non-half-orcs (PHB p.13).

Infravision reaches 12″. Duergar use the standard dwarven underground detection abilities and the dwarven combat abilities against ogres, trolls, ogre magi, giants and titans.
Their save bonus against magical attacks from rods, staves, wands or spells is +1 per 3½ points of Constitution; the same bonus applies against natural poison.
They speak dwarvish, undercommon and their alignment language, plus at most two other languages regardless of Intelligence.
If psionics are used, duergar have twice the usual chance of being psionic: double the Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma bonuses; this does not guarantee psionic ability.

Gray dwarves can be fighters, clerics or thieves; thieves may be assassins or thief-acrobats. The listed multiclass options are fighter/cleric, fighter/thief, cleric/thief and cleric/assassin. PCs may be of any alignment.

rules.title: Duergar light sensitivity
rules.summary: Daylight and continual light negate duergar's enhanced surprise, reduce effective dexterity by 2, impose −2 on attacks and give opponents +2 on saves against their attacks.
bullets: Attacking illuminated opponents from darkness instead imposes −1 to hit and gives targets +1 on those saves.
Ordinary torches, lanterns, magic weapons, light and faerie fire are explicitly too dim to cause this penalty.
Drow use this same light-sensitivity treatment.

rules.title: Drow PCs differ from drow NPCs
rules.summary: A UA drow adventurer does not inherit the NPC's 50% magic resistance or automatic access to underworld armor, weapons and poisons.
bullets: The PC retains elven sleep/charm resistance and gains +2 on saves against magical effects.
Drow do not receive the surface elves' sword and bow attack bonuses.
Two readily one-handed weapons may be used without penalty and without a shield; a spiked buckler may serve as one weapon.
Drow infravision reaches 12″; base movement is 15″ for females and 12″ for males.

Drow detect secret and concealed doors as other elves do, and detect new construction, stonework traps, sliding walls and underground depth as dwarves do. They move silently under the same conditions as other elves and are surprised only 1 in 8.

Drow speak common, undercommon, elvish and gnomish, with further languages limited by Intelligence. Their silent tongue uses signs, expression and body language at a range of 30 feet; only drow fully master it, though others can learn basic signs.

Drow PCs may be clerics, fighters (including rangers), cavaliers, magic-users or thieves (including acrobats and assassins). Male and female level limits differ in cleric, fighter and magic-user classes; consult the separate UA level tables.

At the DM’s option, drow ability scores may use normal generation or the Fiend Folio method. If the latter is used, the PHB initial elf racial adjustments do not apply. The separate Fiend Folio method is not transcribed here.
An adventuring PC drow cannot regain the NPC magic resistance except by wish or similar magic.

Females of 4th level or above may also use clairvoyance, detect lie (or its reverse), suggestion and dispel magic, each once per day.

rules.title: Deep gnome PCs: defenses and limitations
rules.summary: A player-character svirfneblin lacks the NPC's innate magic resistance and automatic AC improvement, but has +2 saves against poison and +3 on other saves.
bullets: The character is immune to illusions and phantasms.
Once-daily blindness, blur and change self use the highest class level; personal non-detection also applies.
PC deep gnomes do not have psionic abilities under this source.

A non-illusionist deep gnome who reaches 6th level in any class can attempt a summon once per day, similar to conjure elemental: roll d20; 1: 24 HD earth elemental; 2–6: 16 HD earth elemental; 7–10: 12 HD earth elemental; 11–15: 8 HD earth elemental; 16–18: xorn; 19–20: failure, with no further attempt that day.
Infravision reaches 12″ and ultravision 3″; bright light reduces all vision to 3″ and imposes −1 to hit opponents in such conditions.
A PC deep gnome is surprised only 1 in 12; it surprises others 9 in 10 when alone or with other deep gnomes and not wearing bulky armor.
Deep underground, it has a 60% chance to camouflage itself against natural rock, remaining effectively invisible until moving, attacking or taking another action that negates invisibility.
In melee against drow and kuo-toa, it gains +1 to hit and damage.
UA describes player-character deep gnomes as male; they may use the classes and class combinations available to surface gnomes.
They use standard gnomish abilities for detecting underground slopes and unsafe walls, and determining underground depth and direction.

They speak their own tongue and may learn other languages according to Intelligence. PCs cannot automatically converse with Elemental Plane of Earth creatures unless they have learned the relevant language, and are as likely to be attacked by them as other races.
Against attacks from giants, bugbears, ogre magi, ogres, trolls or titans, they receive the same benefits as surface gnomes. The underlying surface-gnome rule remains a separate reference.

rules.title: Gray, wood and wild elf distinctions
rules.summary: UA elven sub-races retain many high-elf traits but add specific changes. Gray elves gain +1 intelligence, potentially reaching 19.
bullets: Gray elves share high-elf abilities, including sleep and charm resistance, sword and bow ability, infravision, secret/concealed-door detection and silent movement when alone. They share high-elf languages and add +1 to the initial Intelligence roll, up to 19.

Wood (sylvan) elves have similar elven traits, gain +1 initial Strength (maximum 18) and −1 initial Intelligence. Their starting languages are elvish, common, treant and the tongue of woodland mammals; the passage gives them no other starting languages.

Wild elves (grugach) retain standard elven resistance, weapon bonuses, infravision, silent movement and door detection. They gain +2 initial Strength (maximum 18), deal with woodland creatures as if animal friendship were in effect, and set pits, snares and natural traps with a 90% success chance. Most speak only elvish, though a player character may also know some common.

The UA p.7 class table permits gray elves to be cavaliers, clerics, druids, fighters, rangers, magic-users or thieves (including acrobats and assassins); wood elves have those choices except cavalier; wild elves can be druids, fighters or thieves (including acrobats and assassins). Wild elf multiclassing is restricted to fighter/thief.
These are the UA class choices; ability requirements, multiclass rules and the separate UA class-level limits still apply. Do not merge them with the PHB-only class limits.

UA level-limit table conventions: use Wisdom for cleric/druid, Strength for fighter/ranger/assassin, Intelligence for magic-user, and Dexterity for thief; additional ability requirements appear in footnotes. U means unlimited for the appropriate race/class, subject to the highest level attainable by the class. Below the first score shown, use the lowest listed level; scores above the table do not raise its maximum. If single-classed and that class is an available multiclass choice for the character, the limit may be exceeded by 2. Class eligibility still applies.
UA elf cleric (all except dark elves): Wisdom 12–15: 7; 16: 8; 17: 9; 18: 10; 19: 11; 20–21: 12. Wild elves are not eligible for cleric under UA p.7.
UA elf druid: wild elf Wisdom 12–17: 10; 18: 11; 19: 12; 20: 14, each requiring Charisma 18; 21: 17 requiring Charisma 19. Other elves: U, where class-eligible.

UA elf fighter: Strength 12–17 gives gray/high 5, wild 7, wood 6; 18 gives 6/8/7; 18/75 gives 7/8/8; 18/90 gives 8/10/9; 18/99 gives 9/11/10; 18/00 gives 10/12/11; 19 gives 11/13/12; 20 gives 11/13/14. Values in each group are gray/high, wild, wood respectively.
UA elf magic-user: Intelligence 17–18 gives gray 11 and wood 9; 19 gives 12/10; 20 gives 13/11; 21 gives 15/13; 22 gives 18/13. Wild elves cannot be magic-users under UA p.7.

UA elf thief is U. UA elf assassin: Strength 18, 18/01, 18/51 or 18/76 gives level 10; 18/99 gives 11 with Intelligence 18 and Wisdom 19; 18/00, 19 or 20 gives 12 with Intelligence 19 or Wisdom 19. Apply eligibility separately.

UA elf ranger: Strength 18 gives level 6; 18/01 gives 7 with Intelligence 15 and Wisdom 15, or 8 if both exceed 15; 18/51 gives 9 with Intelligence and Wisdom 16; 18/76, 18/99 or 18/00 gives 10 with Intelligence and Wisdom 17; 19 gives 12 and 20 gives 14, both requiring Intelligence and Wisdom 18. Wild elves cannot be rangers under UA p.7.

rules.title: Ability generation: arrange the best scores
rules.summary: The DMG offers several alternatives to straight 3d6 ability generation; the DM selects the campaign's method.
bullets: Method I: roll 4d6 for each ability score, discard the lowest die, then arrange the six scores.
Method II: roll 3d6 twelve times, keep the highest six totals, then arrange them.

rules.title: Secondary skills are an optional background tool

rules.title: Starting age depends on race and class

rules.title: Wilderness encounters depend on population and terrain
rules.summary: The outdoor procedure varies both the encounter die and the times of day at which it is checked.
bullets: An encounter occurs on 1: use d20 in densely populated country, d12 in moderately to sparsely populated or patrolled areas, and d10 in wilderness.
Check plain in morning, evening and midnight; scrub in morning, evening, night and pre-dawn; desert in morning, night and pre-dawn; hills at noon, night and pre-dawn; mountains in morning and night.
Forest and marsh call for checks in all six periods. For parties over 100 creatures, also check periods marked as otherwise omitted.

bullets: When surprise occurs, subtract the surprise die's indicated value from the distance total.
For each die, subtract 1 from 3s and 4s in scrub, from all rolls in forest, and from 2s, 3s and 4s in marsh; other terrain features can shorten distance further.

rules.title: Check for getting lost before the day's movement

A correct map prevents getting lost under this procedure; mapped landmarks can reveal an error and permit backtracking.
Chance per day: plain 1 in 10; scrub 3; forest 7; rough 3; desert 4; hills 2; mountains 5; marsh 6, each in 10.
When lost, direction is 60° left or right in plain, scrub, rough, desert or hills; in mountains 60° or 120° left or right; in forest or marsh any other hex direction.

Against a ground target, the qualifying dive begins at least 30 feet above it.

rules.title: A charge changes movement, defense and first strike
rules.summary: Indoors, an unencumbered creature charges at double base speed. Outdoors, a biped adds one-third of base speed and a quadruped adds one-half.
bullets: To strike that round, finish within 10 feet. At contact, longer weapon or reach determines first strike; a surviving charger gains +2 to hit.
The charger loses its dexterity AC bonus. With no such bonus its AC worsens by one, except a creature already at AC 10.
Only one charge is allowed per turn, with nine intervening rounds before another.

rules.title: Weapon speed matters for tied melee attacks
rules.summary: When melee opponents tie initiative and both use weapons, the lower weapon speed factor strikes first.
bullets: When speed factor determines order, a difference at least twice the lower factor, or at least 5 in any case, gives the lower-factor weapon two attacks before the higher-factor weapon attacks.
At a difference of 10 or more, the lower-factor weapon gets those two attacks plus one simultaneous with the higher-factor weapon’s attack.
Speed factor is not used to order the initial closing or charging round.
Casting against an attacking weapon uses a separate timing comparison; do not apply one blanket speed-factor bonus to every initiative roll.

rules.title: Dungeon pursuit tracks distance, speed and lost contact
rules.summary: Resolve a dungeon chase by comparing the slowest pursued member with the fastest pursuer and tracking their positions.
bullets: The procedure divides a round into three movement phases; closing to 10 feet produces confrontation.
If the pursued are faster, pursuit ends when they are visible over 100 feet away, leave sight over 50 feet away, or pursuit exceeds 5 rounds without perceptible gain.
At equal speed, the respective limits are over 150 feet visible, over 80 feet when leaving sight, or over 1 turn without perceptible gain.
If pursuers are faster, pursuit ends only when the pursued leave sight over 200 feet away or the pursuers cannot continue for endurance reasons.
Special tracking senses can defeat ordinary attempts to escape; mapping and measured navigation are not available while fleeing.

rules.title: Distractions can break pursuit
rules.summary: Barriers, dropped food or treasure, and branching passages can interrupt a chase, depending on the pursuers' motives and senses.
bullets: Food and treasure are not automatic escape buttons; use the pursuer's intelligence and interests.
At a three-way choice without sight, sound or scent clues, a pursuer has a two-in-three chance of taking the wrong way.

For palatable food or wine offered to pursuers of low intelligence or less, determine a 10%–100% base chance with d10 unless their hunger is known; add 10% per intelligence point below 5. Non-intelligent pursuers have a 100% probability. If the chance is under 100%, roll d10 again to test it; success distracts them for one round.

Treasure can distract pursuers of low intelligence or higher: start at 10%–100%, adding 10% per 10 items for low-intelligence pursuers or 10% per 100 gp of value or potential value for those of average intelligence or more. Test with a second d10; success lasts one round or the time needed to collect the treasure, whichever is longer. Tiny valuables can go unnoticed.

rules.title: Outdoor evasion depends on surprise and terrain
rules.summary: The outdoor evasion procedure starts from an 80% chance, modified by relative speed, terrain, group size and light.
bullets: A party that surprises the monsters can automatically evade; a surprised party cannot evade at that encounter.
Continued pursuit can require new checks each hour.
A faster pursuing group can close within an hour, producing confrontation.
Speed: pursued faster +10%, equal 0%, pursuer faster −20%. Terrain: plain, desert or open water −50%; scrub, rough, hills or marsh +10%; forest or mountains +30%.
Pursued party size: fewer than 6 +10%, 6–11 0%, 12–50 −20%, over 50 −50%. Pursuing party size: fewer than 12 −20%, 12–24 0%, over 24 +10%.
Light: full daylight −30%, twilight −10%, bright moonlight 0%, starlight +20%, dark night +50%.

rules.title: Items save according to material, exposure and magic
rules.summary: An item saving throw applies when the object is actually exposed to the attack. Use the material row and the specific attack form in the item matrix.
bullets: Magical items gain +2, plus another +1 for each enchantment plus above +1; a +2 item therefore gets +3.
An item gains +5 against attacks in its own mode, such as fire against a ring of fire resistance.
Normal fire, magical fire, fireball and electrical attack forms have distinct columns; do not substitute one general damage save.

Read each item sequence as the required d20 score or higher, in order: acid; crushing blow; normal blow; disintegration; fall; fireball or breath; magical fire; normal fire; magical frost; lightning bolt; electrical discharge/current. The table prints 0 and scores above 20; apply relevant adjustments.

Liquid covers potions, magical oils, poisons and acids while the container remains intact; soft metal or jewelry includes pearls. Mirror means silvered glass; use soft-metal or hard-metal rows for silver or steel mirrors.
Hard metal struck forcefully against a very hard surface after extreme cold takes −10 on the die. Nonmagical items also gain +5 against attacks in their own mode.
The fall column assumes a 5-foot fall onto a hard surface: softer wood-like surfaces give +1 and fleshy-soft surfaces +5; each additional 5 feet subtracts 1 from the saving die.
Normal fire requires sufficient exposure: examples give paper/parchment 1 melee round, cloth 2, bone/ivory 3. Other attack forms use the DMG p.80 definitions.

Acid assumes a considerable volume of strong acid or immersion long enough to affect the item. A crushing blow is a heavy impact; a normal blow is from a normal-strength opponent or a fairly heavy object. Disintegration is the magical effect.

Fireball includes a magical fireball, meteor swarm or red-dragon breath; magical fire includes wall of fire, fire storm and flame strike. Magical frost includes cold such as white-dragon breath, cone of cold or ice storm.
Lightning bolt includes magical lightning called from the sky or blue-dragon breath; electrical discharge/current includes electric-eel shock, magical items and traps.

rules.title: Overlapping potions can interact unpredictably
rules.summary: Check the potion-miscibility procedure when potions are physically mixed or when someone drinks another potion while a previous one is still active.
bullets: The DM makes the compatibility check secretly.
01: Explosion; internal damage 6–60 hp and those within 5″ take 1–10 hp. If mixed externally, all within 10 feet take 4–24 hp, no save.
02–03: Lethal poison kills the imbiber; if mixed externally, a 10-foot-diameter poison cloud requires those within to save versus poison or die.
04–08: Nausea and −1 strength and dexterity for 5–20 rounds, no save; one potion is cancelled and the other has half strength and duration, determined randomly.
09–15: Both potions are cancelled. 16–25: One randomly selected potion is cancelled and the other remains normal. 26–35: Both are at half efficacy.

36–90: Both work normally unless contradictory effects cancel. 91–99: One randomly selected potion has 150% efficacy, subject to the DM deciding whether effect and duration or only duration may increase.
00: One potion functions permanently on the imbiber; harmful side effects are possible.

fields.Material: Brass brazier with charcoal, 100 gp of incense, herbs including basil/savory/catnip, and fat

matrices.title: Original attack matrix: fighters, paladins, rangers, and related attackers
notes: All 210 cells of matrix I.B were checked against the supplied revised December 1979 Dungeon Masters Guide scan.
The table applies to fighters, paladins, and rangers. Bards use their highest attained fighter level, not their current bard level. Its separate level-0 column applies to halflings and humans.

A cell is the table's 20-sided-die target for the named attacker level band and opponent armor class, before resolving applicable adjustments. It is not automatically equivalent to AC-zero target minus armor class.
The original table repeats 20 in some columns, so a single linear THAC0 subtraction can disagree with it. The examples below use only cells actually legible in this scan.
Any current group convention using simple THAC0 remains a group choice; this reference does not silently replace that convention or the printed matrix.

ruleNotes.title: Missile range adjustments
ruleNotes.text: The matrix prints a −2 adjustment at medium missile range and −5 at long range.

ruleNotes.title: Optional per-level fighter progression
ruleNotes.text: The DM may choose a +1 to-hit bonus at the second level within each two-level fighter band, producing the source's optional per-level progression instead of the ordinary two-level steps. Do not silently apply this option.

ruleNotes.title: Certain spell adjustments change AC
ruleNotes.text: For the listed kinds of spell effects, including curse, prayer, and protection from evil, the DMG instructs the referee to adjust the relevant armor class rather than reduce the attack die result. This preserves the intended repeated-20 behavior. This note is about those spell adjustments, not a universal conversion of every modifier into AC.

ruleNotes.title: Repeated 20s and a separate natural-20 option
ruleNotes.text: The DMG explains the repeated 20s as part of the printed combat-table progression. It then offers an optional amendment: second and later repeated-20 entries require a natural 20, and targets above 20 require a natural 20 plus sufficient bonus. The initial 20 entry still permits die result plus bonuses. Keep that amendment distinct from the unamended printed table; do not infer an unconditional natural-20 rule from it.

comparisonExamples.explanation: With no additional adjustments in this illustration, the original matrix's repeated 20 differs from the linear calculation 20 − (−1).
The source-listed cell is 20; a simple AC-zero subtraction would produce 24. No missing cells were generated from that formula.

coverage.method: The 210 cells were read against printed DMG page 74 and independently compared; this check is limited to the matrix cells.
coverage.missingCellsMeaning: A null indicates an unavailable value; it never means an impossible hit or a target score of zero.

classes.name: Cavalier
classes.description: A chivalric mounted-warrior class with social qualifications, possible zero-level stages, and its own conduct code. The original table's hit-die heading conflicts with other text; errata must be identified separately.
guidance: Requires Strength, Dexterity, Constitution 15 and Intelligence, Wisdom 10; confirm service, social station, sponsorship, and any zero-level stages.
At each higher level, increase the Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution percentiles by the specified 2d10 procedure.
Below the self-training threshold, train with a cavalier of at least level 4 or two levels higher, whichever is greater.
After reaching level 6, the normal regimen suffices for training; mount and weapon abilities continue to change.

classes.name: Thief-acrobat
classes.description: A specialist path entered after ordinary thief levels. Its specialist XP thresholds and conversion procedure are supplied.
guidance: Requires Strength 15 and Dexterity 16, and five completed thief levels.
On qualifying for level 6, train for six weeks under a thief-acrobat of at least level 10.
Pick pockets, opening locks, and finding/removing traps stop improving at their level-5 ability; magical writing is never gained.
Use the specialist acrobatics tables and the continuing climb-walls ability; the future growth of the other retained thief skills needs a campaign ruling on UA p. 23.

changes: Under the ordinary-thief progression retained by UA p. 25, add one d6 hit die with the applicable Constitution adjustment (minimum 1 hp after penalties).
Climb walls explicitly continues under UA p. 23: base chance 90% → 92% before applicable adjustments.
After five ordinary thief levels and sufficient XP for sixth, complete six weeks with a thief-acrobat trainer of at least level 10.

Strength 15 and Dexterity 16 are required. If both scores are at least 16, earned XP gains a 10% bonus.

Tightrope walking permits upright travel with hands free at 60 feet per round, checking again for each distance beyond 60 feet. Ordinary moderate/strong winds impose −10/−20 percentage points; strong gusts retain a 5% failure chance.

Pole vaulting needs a 30-foot run and a pole at least 4 feet taller than you. High jumps and running broad jumps need a 20-foot run; apply the specialist distances rather than ordinary-thief distances.
The stated sixth-level falling example gives a 25% chance to avoid damage from a 10-foot fall; if damage occurs, take 75% of the normal damage, rounded down.
Tumbling attack bonuses apply to pummeling. Evasion requires initiative in the situations described and cannot exceed a 60% base before Dexterity/race adjustments.

Keep body-associated equipment within the current level’s encumbrance limit to vault, jump, or tumble. A backpack is disallowed during acrobatics except tightrope walking; carried loot usually needs to be droppable.

progression.label: Thief specialist path
progression.description: After five ordinary thief levels, a character with Strength 15+ and Dexterity 16+ may specialize on qualifying for level 6. Training takes six weeks with a thief-acrobat of at least level 10. UA calls this a “split-class” specialist and otherwise treats it as a thief except for the stated changes; it has its own specialist advancement table.

classes.name: Druid · UA high levels
classes.description: UA extends the druid hierarchy through Grand Druid and a separate Hierophant progression. The XP reset makes a simple level-1 cumulative array unsuitable.
guidance: The Grand Druid is level 15, with at least 3,000,001 XP; the office carries special responsibilities and benefits.
After at least 3,500,001 XP, a Grand Druid may seek a successor and abdicate.
On entering the level-16 Hierophant path, the XP total resets to 1 and office-related bonus spells are relinquished.
Use the separate Hierophant table and planar abilities; do not extrapolate the PHB druid table.

changes: Grand Druid eligibility begins at 3,000,001 XP; the office knows six spells of each spell level and gains the stated extra six spell levels, subject to the unique office and service conditions.
After at least 3,500,001 XP as Grand Druid, find a successor and abdicate to enter the Hierophant path: reset XP to 1 and relinquish the office-related extra spell levels.
Spell-slot maxima stay at six per spell level; future advancement changes casting level and grants special powers instead of additional slots.
Gain immunity to natural animal/vegetable poisons (including monster poisons), but not mineral poisons or poison gas; gain 160 extra years of life and vigorous health.

You can alter appearance non-magically in 1 segment: height and weight up to 50% either way, apparent age from child to very old, and human/humanoid features; true seeing or similar perception can reveal it.

For elemental conjuring, UA replaces the earth results and supplies further tables. A roll equal to or below your level as a percentage selects the desired creature type; otherwise roll the appropriate result normally.
Druid casting level increases 16 → 17; daily slots remain six at each spell level 1–7. Extra longevity increases 160 → 170 years.
Gain hibernation/suspended animation without aging for up to the longevity period (170 years at this level).

progression.label: Advanced XP reset track
progression.description: Continues the druid class through Grand Druid and Hierophant. After reaching at least 3,500,001 XP, a Grand Druid who finds a successor may abdicate and enter the level-16 Hierophant category with XP reset to 1. The reset begins a separate advancement scale within this druid progression.

progressionExplainer.title: Class tracks, combinations, and special paths
progressionExplainer.description: These labels describe the progression represented by each guide. Check race, abilities, alignment, and campaign requirements in the cited rules before choosing a character’s classes.

sections.label: Concurrent multiclass
sections.description: PHB pp. 32–33 presents combinations operated at the same time by non-human or semi-human characters. The combinations available depend on race; this is a separate procedure from changing professions.

sections.label: Sequential class change (dual-class)
sections.description: PHB p. 33’s human-only profession change stops advancement in the former class. It requires principal attribute scores of at least 15 in the original class and 17 or 18 in the new class, with alignment restrictions. The character retains earlier hit points but begins the new class’s other functions at level 1. Former-class functions restrict new-class XP until the new level exceeds the old one.

sections.label: Special published progressions
sections.description: The bard appendix supplies a fighter → thief → bard sequence. UA supplies a thief-acrobat specialist path and an advanced druid track with an XP reset. Each follows its own cited transition rules; their labels do not grant general permission to combine classes.

terminologyNotes: “Dual-class” is a navigation gloss here. PHB p. 33 heads its sequential rule “The Character With Two Classes.”

The bard appendix permits humans and half-elves, while the general two-class rule requires a human. The bard guide is classified by its appendix sequence rather than automatically assigned that general procedure.
For the bard’s thief-stage transition, PHB p. 117 says “between 5th and 9th.” This metadata retains that wording without resolving its boundary convention.
UA p. 23 calls thief-acrobat a “split-class” specialist; UA p. 25 otherwise treats the specialist as a thief except for the stated changes.
A Class track badge identifies one guide’s advancement table; it makes no finding about eligibility for a permitted race-based class combination.
